name: Amasai
overview: Amasai was a male Levite belonging to the Kohathite clan, identified specifically as the son of Elkanah. His lineage is noted in 1 Chronicles 6:25 and 6:35, situating him within the tribe of Levi, a tribe set apart for priestly and temple duties. This connection highlights his role within the Levitical heritage.
namesAndTitles: The name Amasai means '[my] people are from Jesse,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin as recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:25. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful connection to the people and heritage implied in its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Amasai as the son of Elkanah (1 Chronicles 6:25) and infers Mahath as his father (1 Chronicles 6:35). Beyond these relationships, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Amasai's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogy, particularly the Kohathite branch, which was responsible for specific sacred duties related to the tabernacle and temple. His identification as son of Elkanah situates him within the priestly lineage that contributed to the worship and service of God in Israel. Though not elaborated on in detail, his mention affirms the continuity of Levitical service and heritage essential to the biblical narrative of God's covenant people.
